readme.html:
Seatback Cinema: inflight movie picker

Seatback Cinema is a GitHub dataset of the in-flight entertainment (IFE) catalogs of 11 airlines, Emirates ice, United and British Airways among them, with every film matched to IMDb, plus an agent skill that ranks what's on your flight by IMDb and Letterboxd ratings and your own taste. Ask Claude (in the app, or Claude Code), Codex or Cursor "what should I watch on my Emirates flight?" and it answers from the films Emirates is actually showing that month.

Also searched as: seatback-cinema, flightflix, skyflix, planeflix, inflight movie finder, airline movie ranker, mile-high movies, cabin cinema, airline movie list ranked by IMDb.

Airlines

October 2026, from public/data/index.json. "Films" counts each film once, even where the airline lists it once per audio track. "IMDb id" is the share matched with high or medium confidence.

airline id films IMDb id
Emirates (ice) emirates 2,055 93.1%
Cathay Pacific cathay 1,551 91.6%
American Airlines american 682 95.3%
British Airways ba 658 95.1%
United Airlines united 508 96.3%
KLM klm 474 96.6%
Lufthansa lufthansa 405 97.0%
Singapore Airlines singapore 384 94.0%
Qantas qantas 257 87.2%
ANA ana 233 93.1%
Japan Airlines jal 124 88.7%

7,331 films in all, 6,862 of them with an IMDb id.

Use it in the Claude app (web and mobile)

Seatback Cinema is a Claude plugin, installed from this repo in one step on claude.ai (paid plans): Customize, Plugins, Add, Add marketplace, and enter len5ky/seatback-cinema; then install Seatback Cinema. It's saved to your account, so the mobile and desktop apps get it too.

The plugin is a skill plus the Seatback Cinema connector. The skill alone is enough: it reads the catalogue and your taste from https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/. Adding the connector from the plugin's Connectors tab (one click, no login) is optional; it lets you paste an IMDb or Letterboxd export into the chat and keeps working when Claude's web fetch is unavailable.

No plugins on your plan? The skill also comes as a zip, https://seatback.len5ky.com/inflight-movie-picker-web.zip: upload it, unopened, at Customize, Skills.

After that, start a chat, on the web or in the mobile app, and say where you're flying. Any of these works:

I'm on Emirates to Dubai on Thursday, about 7 hours. My IMDb ratings are at https://www.imdb.com/user/ur12345678/ratings/. Skip anything I've already seen and pick me three films for the flight, newer ones first.

Flying United to Chicago tomorrow, 9 hours, no idea what's on. Show me what's good and ask me what I've seen.

BA to New York with two kids, 8 and 11. What's on board for them, and one thing for me after they fall asleep?

Is Project Hail Mary on Qantas this month? If not, what's the closest thing?

Claude drops what you've seen and answers with three films and a backup, each with its ratings, a one-line synopsis, why it suits you and an IMDb link. For your taste it asks for a public IMDb profile link first, then a Letterboxd username, then a taste code from last time. With none of those, it lists ten likely picks, twice, and drops the ones you say you've seen.

The taste code. https://seatback.len5ky.com/taste reads your IMDb or Letterboxd export in the browser and gives you a 20-character code; nothing goes through the chat. Paste the sentence it shows ("My Seatback Cinema taste code is ...") and Claude skips everything you've rated. The code holds film ids and your scores, nothing else, for a year. Claude also offers to make one after the first import in a chat.

The IMDb link. Your ratings have to be public (Settings, Privacy on imdb.com). Seatback reads them on its own server, scores and watchlist included, and keeps the import for a day; Letterboxd gives it only your latest 50 diary entries. When a link fails, an IMDb export (CSV, from https://www.imdb.com/list/ratings/export on a computer) or a Letterboxd export (zip) still works, attached to the chat (with the connector) or turned into a code at https://seatback.len5ky.com/taste.

Quick start: the skill

In Claude Code, the same plugin installs with one command and brings the connector with it:

/plugin install seatback-cinema --marketplace len5ky/seatback-cinema

For Codex, Cursor and other agents, or for a Claude Code without network tools, there is a second skill, skill/inflight-movie-picker: a SKILL.md and a dependency-free script that downloads one airline-month from the open dataset and prints it as a table (Bun, Node 22.6+ or Deno). Install it straight from GitHub:

npx skills add len5ky/seatback-cinema          # asks which agent to install it for

Or fetch the folder yourself, no clone needed:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/len5ky/seatback-cinema/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz \
  | tar xz -C ~/.codex/skills --strip-components=2 seatback-cinema-main/skill/inflight-movie-picker     # Codex CLI

Start a new session and ask about your flight; the four prompts in the Claude app section above work here too. For Cursor, copy the folder into your project and add a rule that points at its SKILL.md; skill/README.md has the rule file and the Codex fallback for versions that don't load skills.

The skill asks for the airline, flight length, who's watching and the mood, then gives three films and a backup on a long-haul flight, one or two under 110 minutes on a short one, and family titles only when kids are watching. Each pick carries its IMDb link. If you have no export to hand it asks for five films you loved and two you hated.

What a pick looks like

This is the project's own CLI on the October Emirates catalogue, with an IMDb export imported (bun run cli picks --airline emirates --min-year 2025 --top 3):

Emirates 2026-10: top 3 picks (excluded: 58 low-confidence, 94 unmatched, 254 already watched)
taste: 938 ratings (mean 7.3/10), 938 watched, 103 on watchlist; taste.json as overrides

 1. Obsession (2025)  Horror, Thriller  109 min  IMDb 7.8 (414k)  LB 4.1  RT 94%  score 9.46
    A hopeless romantic's wish for true love spirals into a nightmare in this breakout horror hit.
    why: on your watchlist; you rate horror -0.5 (49 films); Curry Barker; English; https://www.imdb.com/title/tt37287335/ (high)
 2. Sawt Hind Rajab (2025)  Drama  84 min  IMDb 8.2 (22k)  LB 4.4  RT 100%  score 8.77
    An award-winning true story drama about a young girl's call for help and the race to reach her.
    why: Kaouther Ben Hania; Arabic; https://www.imdb.com/title/tt36943034/ (medium)
 3. I Swear (2025)  Drama, Comedy  120 min  IMDb 8.3 (72k)  LB 4.3  RT 98%  score 8.65
    A BAFTA®-winning biopic of pioneering Tourette syndrome activist John Davidson.
    why: Kirk Jones; English; https://www.imdb.com/title/tt31514146/ (high)

The skills present picks in the same card shape. In the Claude app the ratings come from the connector. The coding-agent skill has no scraped ratings, so its numbers come from the model's knowledge of the film and, when TMDB_API_KEY is set, from TMDB.

Add your taste

An export beats any interview: films you've rated drop out, your watchlist floats up, and the model sees what you loved and hated.

  • IMDb: sign in at imdb.com, open your name menu (top right), then Your ratings. Click the three-dot menu above the list and choose Export. IMDb builds the CSV and lists it under Your exports, where you download it. Do the same from your Watchlist. Put the files in data/imdb-ratings/ in the folder you start the agent from.
  • Letterboxd: letterboxd.com, Settings, the Data tab, Export your data. Unzip the download anywhere and tell the agent where it is.
  • No export: give the agent your public profile URL. The script reads it with --imdb-url or --letterboxd-url from your own machine. IMDb often refuses scripted requests, and the script then points you back to the export.

IMDb rows join on the IMDb id, so they never mismatch. Letterboxd exports carry no IMDb id, so those join on title and year, which can miss a retitled film.

Limits

  • Not covered: Delta (its public pages show about 80 of roughly 300 films, title and poster only), Turkish (10 highlights behind PerimeterX), Air France (no public catalogue) and Qatar (the catalogue sits behind Akamai and only loads in a real browser).
  • Twice a month. The data refreshes on the 1st and 15th. BA, Singapore, Qantas and American only publish the current cycle, so next month's line-up for them appears once it starts.
  • One catalogue per airline. Routes, aircraft and cabins differ. Qantas is the large international seatback set; a domestic 737 shows less.
  • Medium-confidence matches. About 7% of IMDb ids rest on a single signal, often runtime alone. The skill flags them; check the link before you trust the rating. Regional-language films and concert specials match least often, and unmatched films are left out of rankings rather than guessed.

API

Everything the skill and the connector do is available as plain GET requests at https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/, as JSON with open CORS. Picks come back as the same cards the connector returns. Add pretty=1 to indent the output.

curl 'https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/airlines'
curl 'https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/picks?airline=emirates&flight_minutes=420&min_year=2025&limit=3&pretty=1'
curl 'https://seatback.len5ky.com/api/picks?airline=emirates&imdb=https://www.imdb.com/user/ur12345678/ratings/&limit=3'

/api/catalogue takes airline, genre (comma-separated), min_year, max_year, max_runtime, family, q, limit and offset. /api/picks takes airline, flight_minutes, the same filters, limit, and one of imdb (a profile link or its ur / p. id), letterboxd (a username) or code (a taste code). /api/profile?imdb=... imports a profile and returns { code, rated, watchlist }. Errors come back as { error, hint } with a 4xx or 5xx status.

Limits: an IMDb profile can be imported 10 times a UTC day, and all profiles together 2,000 times. An import is kept for 24 hours, so repeat calls with the same link cost nothing. Letterboxd covers the latest 50 diary entries. picks returns at most 20 films and catalogue 200 rows a page. Calls without a profile are cached for 5 minutes; calls with one are never cached. Taste codes last a year.

For developers

Dataset

public/data/index.json                 airlines, months, film counts, fetch times
public/data/<airline>/<YYYY-MM>.json   one catalogue
public/data/ids.json                   IMDb id -> TMDB, Letterboxd, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic ids
public/data/health.json                last fetch attempt per airline: status, film count, error tail

Each film has sourceId, title, year, runtime, directors, genres, rating, languages, categories, imdbId, imdbConfidence, tmdbId. rating is the airline's age classification. imdbId is set only for high and medium matches. Read it from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/len5ky/seatback-cinema/main/public/data/index.json.

Licence: the files in public/data/ are released under CC0 1.0. They hold catalogue metadata only. No synopses, posters, cast lists or ratings are redistributed; ratings stay in the local database and the data links out to IMDb and TMDB instead. Titles and listings come from the airlines' public sites. IMDb ids come from IMDb's non-commercial datasets, whose terms still apply to anything you build on them. ids.json comes from Wikidata, also CC0.

Running the pipeline

Needs Bun; bun install pulls dev types only, storage is the built-in bun:sqlite.

bun run cli fetch <airline|all> [--month 2026-11] [--refresh]  # monthly catalogue -> data/plane_movie.sqlite
bun run cli imdb sync [--force]    # download IMDb datasets (~1.2 GB, refreshed when >7 days old) and load them
bun run cli match [--airline X]    # match catalogue films to IMDb titles
bun run cli stats [--airline X]    # film count and match rate by confidence
bun run cli picks [--airline emirates] [--top 30] [--genre Thriller] [--min-rating 7] [--language English] [--min-year 2020] [--max-year 2025] [--year 2025] [--month YYYY-MM] [--full]
bun run cli search "toy story" [--airline X]   # which airlines carry it this month
bun run cli export [--month 2026-10] [--airline X]  # public/data/<airline>/<month>.json, ids.json, index.json
bun run cli taste import [file ...]            # IMDb CSVs and/or a Letterboxd zip (default: data/imdb-ratings/, data/letterboxd/)
bun run cli ids sync [--airline X] [--limit N] # Wikidata crosswalk to TMDB / Letterboxd / RT / Metacritic ids
bun run cli ratings sync [--source tmdb|letterboxd|rt|mc|all] [--airline X] [--limit N]
bun run serve                                  # public/ on http://localhost:4173 (SEATBACK_PORT to change)

bun run cli with no arguments prints this list and the registered airline ids. bun test runs the unit tests (fixtures in tests/fixtures/ are real responses with synopses, cast and image URLs stripped) and bun run typecheck typechecks.

bun run serve also lets you try the skill on a fresh export before anything is pushed: SEATBACK_DATASET_URL=http://localhost:4173 or --base public points the skill's script at it.

public/index.html is a static leaderboard (film counts, match rate, fetch health per airline) that reads the same files; bun run serve and open http://localhost:4173.

Ratings and taste in the CLI

Picks score on a 10-point scale. The public part blends IMDb (0.4), Letterboxd average (0.3, stars x2), RT audience (0.15) and Metascore (0.15). IMDb is pulled toward 6.5 by min_votes, IMDb and Letterboxd weights scale with log10 of their vote counts, and a missing source drops out with the rest re-normalised.

Taste comes from bun run cli taste import. Every film you rated adds its deviation from your mean rating to its genres and directors; an affinity is that sum divided by (films + 3), so one film moves it a little and ten move it a lot. Watched films are excluded, watchlist films get +1.5, and the strongest affinities show up as reasons ("you rate horror -0.5 (49 films)"). taste.json stays as manual overrides: liked and disliked genres, favourites, seen, min_rating, min_votes.

Letterboxd, RT and Metacritic are scraped at one request per second per site with a 30-day cache, for personal use only: Letterboxd's terms forbid automated access, and none of those scores is ever exported. TMDB needs TMDB_API_KEY in .env (free from themoviedb.org, Settings, API).

Publishing

.github/workflows/monthly.yml runs at 05:17 UTC on the 1st and 15th, and on manual dispatch with an optional month. It loads IMDb, runs scripts/fetch-all.sh (each airline with a 20-minute timeout; one failure doesn't stop the rest), then match, ids sync and export. scripts/build-index.ts rebuilds index.json from the files on disk, so an airline that failed keeps its last good month. The Actions bot commits public/data to main with [skip ci] through scripts/push-dataset.sh. A run takes 10 to 20 minutes, mostly Lufthansa, JAL and ANA, which make one request per film.

American answers HTTP 429 to GitHub runner IPs, so CI skips it. scripts/american-local.sh runs from a crontab on the maintainer's machine at 03:00 UTC on the same days: it fetches American, matches, exports that airline and pushes from its own worktree (tmp/american-publish), rebasing over CI's commit if both land at once. --dry-run stops before the push.

Adding an airline

Every adapter implements AirlineAdapter from src/airlines/types.ts:

fetchMonth(month: string, opts: { cacheDir: string; refresh?: boolean }): Promise<unknown>; // cache raw responses under cacheDir/<id>/<month>/
parse(raw: unknown): CatalogueFilm[];                                                         // pure, deduped

fetchMonth saves every HTTP response and reuses it unless --refresh; an airline with no month selector refuses any month but the current one. parse is pure and gets a unit test against a saved response in tests/fixtures/ with synopses, cast and image URLs stripped. Fill year and directors whenever the source has them: the matcher leans on both. Register the adapter in src/airlines/index.ts. Keep it low-volume: one fetch per airline-month per day, no retry loops. Gee Media Airtime (United, KLM, Cathay Pacific) and Spafax (Lufthansa, JAL) already have shared clients in src/airlines/platforms/, so an airline on either platform is mostly configuration.

airline source requests per fetch
Emirates emirates.com/service/exp/ice JSON 2
United, KLM Gee Media Airtime API 2
British Airways entertainment.ba.com/api proxy (Akamai, browser UA) ~20
Singapore KrisWorld catalog-lookup 1
Lufthansa, JAL Spafax API, one detail call per film ~410, ~130
Cathay Pacific Anuvu AirTime (Airtime client, other base URL) ~38
Qantas qantas.com/api/entertainment/metadata 1
ANA CineSend search plus one detail call per title ~235
American entertainment.aa.com pages in headless Chromium (plain HTTP is blocked on TLS fingerprint) 25 pages

The matcher

IMDb's title.basics, title.akas, title.ratings, title.crew and name.basics go into SQLite, about 1.3 million titles. An airline that sends an IMDb id (American does) is trusted when IMDb knows the id. Everything else is matched on a normalised title (lowercase, no accents or punctuation, no leading article, roman numerals as digits), with fallbacks for "Marvel's" prefixes, either side of a colon or a trailing parenthesis, and titles cut off with "...". Each candidate is scored on year (exact or one off), director surname (typo-tolerant) and runtime (within 3 minutes). Two agreeing signals and no conflict make a high match, one makes medium, and anything weaker is low or none and never ranked. Emirates sends no year on 72% of its rows, so it leans on director and runtime.

Skills in this repo

  • skill/inflight-movie-picker/ is the public skill described above. It reads the published dataset, so nobody needs the pipeline.
  • plugins/seatback-cinema/skills/inflight-movie-picker-web/ is the Claude app version (shipped as the seatback-cinema plugin): no script, it calls the connector at https://seatback.len5ky.com/mcp. scripts/package-web-skill.sh zips it for upload.
  • .claude/skills/inflight-movie-picker/ is the maintainer's skill for a checkout: it drives the CLI and the local SQLite database, scraped ratings included.
